A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StrSR study. All 18 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2 are readable, including equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original super-resolution evaluations on DIV2K-val, RealSR, and RealLQ250, component ablations, qualitative comparisons, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, qualitative comparisons, and inference-time measurements in Tables 1–4 and the figures.

M1.justification: The dual encoder, DiT generator, CLIP-ConvNeXt discriminator, losses, and one-step generation procedure remain unchanged. The corrected decoding expression in Section 3.3 aligns with integrated-latent decoding already described in v1 Section 3.2, rather than establishing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions train on LSDIR and Aesthetic-4K and evaluate ×4 super-resolution on DIV2K-val, RealSR, and RealLQ250. No additional tested domain or scenario accompanies the new text-region limitation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3, the qualitative comparisons, and Figure 12. Newly cited related works are not new evaluated baselines; StableSR already appears in v1's runtime comparison.

E3.justification: Data selection, degradation processing, evaluation metrics, full-image ×4 testing, model configurations, and training budgets are retained. The newly specified precision, update ratio, and noise parameter document existing training rather than explicitly revise previously stated settings.

E4.justification: The FDL feature visualizations, GAN/VLM ablations, and qualitative cases are retained in Section 4.3, Table 4, and Figures 6–11. The limitations section adds discussion without a new robustness test or failure-case analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the results. The newly disclosed R1 noise parameter is a training detail, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4, runtime values in Figure 12, and illustrated results are unchanged. Section 4.5 newly reports reduced effectiveness in text-rich regions as a qualitative finding, without accompanying measurements or examples.

T1.justification: After Equation 7, v2 corrects x_pred from D_VAE(G_theta(z_LR,t,z_VLM)) to D_VAE(z_LR − t G_theta(z_LR,t,z_VLM)), restoring the latent residual and time scaling. The remaining flow equations and loss formulations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about asymmetric distillation, spectral artifact suppression, the dual encoder, and state-of-the-art one-step restoration. The added limitations do not rewrite these central claims.

C2.justification: New Section 4.5 acknowledges deployment constraints from large backbones, imperfect PSNR/SSIM fidelity, and text-region weakness attributed to the absence of explicit text input. Section 4.1 also explains Qwen3/VLM representation compatibility as the rationale for the frozen VLM and adaptive projection.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies bf16 training, a 1:1 generator/discriminator update ratio, and Gaussian perturbation parameter sigma=0.005 for approximated R1. It expands the VLM integration explanation; the promised code/model release and access location remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for StableSR, HAODiff, OSDFace, and Qwen3-VL, modestly broadening the acceleration discussion to low-level restoration tasks. Qwen3 remains the same cited work; publication metadata updates and consolidation of duplicate AdamW references do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds Limitations and Acknowledgements sections, expands implementation prose, corrects wording such as 'Preliminarys' and 'degeneration,' and updates affiliation and corresponding-author information. The overall narrative and most paragraphs remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 uses wider page margins and reflows existing material. Figure 10 moves from page 13 to 14, while Figures 11–12 and Table 4 move from page 14 to 15. Figure and table content is retained, with only small caption and citation edits.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical consistency through the decoding-formula correction, reproducibility through additional training details, and transparency through explicit deployment and restoration limitations. These are useful, limited gains; the experimental evidence and central claims remain essentially unchanged.
